validator: draft 1 passes (no problems, soft or warnings); the faults below are the critic's.
keep: The idea is named up front in two plain sentences (the work is the area under the pV curve; bars add it up, the reverse rule gets it exactly as (p1V1 - p2V2) / (n - 1)), built from what Dan has: bars and the mid-ordinate rule (lesson 8), the reverse rule and its one gap at power -1 (lesson 7).
The causal step for work = p x dV is there: force p x A, distance d, volume change A x d, so the piston's area drops out; and kPa x m3 = kJ is shown from N/m2 x m3 = N m.

One fully worked example with real numbers from the rule: 400 kPa at 0.1 m3, n = 2, C = 4, 100 kPa at 0.2 m3; 4, 8 and 100 mid-ordinate bars give 19.82, 19.95, 20.00 kJ (recomputed: 19.822, 19.955, 19.9997) and the rule gives (40 - 20) / 1 = 20 kJ. The derivation from C V^-n through V^(1-n)/(1-n) to (p1V1 - p2V2)/(n - 1) is complete, each step with its reason.

Every misconception the brief names for lesson 9 has a DO screen with its own slip: p x V at one point or the whole volume (steps 1, 2, 4, 12), dividing by n or not at all (6, 11), the compression counted as plus (8), the work-on-gas sign form (11), the mean effective pressure as the average of the ends or divided by the end volume (9, 10). Hand-checked: 40, 60; 30, 45, 15; 12.8, 32; 80, 40, 26.7; -20; -80, 80, -40; 200, 250; 266.7, 200, 450; 72, -72, 24; 20 + 15 = 35, 30; practice 164.9, 33.0, 56.7, 24.7, 150, 378.

Twelve screens alternate SHOW (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) and DO (2, 4, 6, 8, 10) and end on two mixed puzzles (11, 12); the n and end-volume sliders and the compression switch from the brief's picture are all there, and the 100 bars agree with the rule to within 0.003 kJ across the whole slider grid.
fix: Faithful to sources: 'Your syllabus draws the curve as pV^n = C' and 'your maths syllabus asks you to derive' assume Dan's college uses the MCA papers, which the brief lists as UNCONFIRMED. Name it as the MCA's second-engineer maths syllabus.

Causal step skipped: 'In a real cylinder the pressure falls as the gas expands' gives no reason. Add one plain-words picture (the same gas spread through more room presses less on each square metre), marked as a way to picture it, not a cited law.

Causal step skipped: 'The reverse rule works for this power too' is asserted. Show it by differentiating back with the power rule, as lesson 7 checks its answers: V^(1-n) / (1 - n) gives (1 - n) V^-n / (1 - n) = V^-n.

Misconception not shown failing: the compression paragraph states the sign but never shows the slip going wrong. Show counting the squeeze as plus: out and back to the same state would hand out 40 kJ from nothing.

Unreadable label and a step Dan cannot do: 'End pressure 800 / 0.4^1.5 x 0.1^1.5' and the practice's (0.05 / 0.2)^1.3 lean on an index law he has not met. Work the end pressure the lesson's own way: C first, then C / V2^n (C = 25.30 then 25.30 / 0.253 = 100 kPa; C = 20.35 then 20.35 / 0.1234 = 164.9 kPa).

Recommended shape, the brief's wording: mean effective pressure is 'area / length'. Say that on the diagram it is the area divided by its length along the volume axis, so it ties to the indicator card.
Thin research: [7] is a course's slide notes, not 'a textbook'. Call it an engineering course's notes.
Analogy wording: a battery does not 'take' 24 J to move 2 C; it gives the charge 24 J. Fix the verb.
ignores carries the n = 1 condition, which the rules say goes with the result; it is already in explain and practice. Drop it from ignores.
verdict: Rewrite as draft 2 with these nine fixes; nothing else needs to change.
